plan.evidence: Quartz Creek Trail to Curry Gap, up the NE ridge across the Pride Glacier, then Class 3 rock on the glacier's left edge to the summit via its SE corner.

headline: F
Class 2
plan.evidence: East Ridge from La Bohn Gap is a Class 2 route, listed as the easiest on the peak.

headline: WI4-5
WI4-5
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Guinness WI4-5.

headline: WI3-4
WI3-4
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Rainier Light WI3-4.

headline: Class 2-3
Class 2
plan.evidence: Lake Mountain is a class 2 scramble with route finding (no single move needs hands); several gullies of similar difficulty.

headline: 4th class
Class 4
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Classic Route 4th class; the easiest route on Lane is class 4 scrambling (steep upper class 3 with a 4th-class finish).

headline: WI2
WI2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: The Zipper WI2 M2 Steep Snow, Grade II, 3 pitches, about 45°.

headline: WI2 / AI1
AI1
plan.evidence: Mountain Project lists The Fly as 'Mod. Snow', the easiest of the three couloirs; the record's breakdown has AI1 with one WI2-/AI1+ step.

headline: AI1
AI1
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Lover's Lane AI1 Mod. Snow; the steepest and narrowest of the three couloirs.

headline: Class 4
Class 4
plan.evidence: From Yang Yang Lakes: a loose gully to the north ridge (one option a high-4th-class chossy gully), then the Le Conte Glacier and an exposed ledge finish.

headline: 5.10a
5.10b
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Spontaneous Distraction 5.10a/b, 4 pitches.
Goatshead Spire (Goodman/Mason, 1982) is listed with no grade; MP notes that Lemah's summits all have class 4-low 5th routes.
MP: 5.13+ Grade IV, 10 pitches, P4 5.13+ crux; Climbing.com reports 5.13d for the FA.
MP: Beckey Route (SW Face) 5.6, 4 pitches.

headline: 5.12a
5.12a
plan.evidence: MP: The Independence Route 5.12a, 12 pitches.
MP: Overexposure 5.8, 2 pitches.
MP: Serpentine Crack 5.11, 4 pitches.
MP: Sidewinder (Southwest Corner) 5.9+, Grade II, 5 pitches; P3a wide flaring crack is the crux.

before.grade: Grade IV, 5.12 free (orig. aid V, 5.9 A3)

plan.evidence: MP: 5.12 Grade IV, 11 pitches; three short 5.12 sections on P5-P6, rest 5.11 and under.

before.grade: Grade V, 5.11a (or 5.9 A3 original aid; 5.13- fully free)

headline: 5.11a
5.11a
plan.evidence: MP: 5.11a C2 Grade V, 12 pitches; the Lithuanian Lip (P2) is aided at C2 (5.13- free).

headline: AI2-3
AI3
plan.evidence: MP: Liberty Ridge Grade IV, AI2-3 steep snow; crux is the steep ice above Thumb Rock / Black Pyramid.
MP: Ptarmigan Ridge 5.6, Grade IV, AI2-3 steep snow; trip reports give IV, 55-degree snow/ice AI2/WI2, 5.6/M3.

headline: Class 2-3 rock
Class 3
plan.evidence: Described as a rock scramble via the Southeast Ridge to the Lichtenhorn; the craggy west summit is reported as Class 3.

headline: Class 3
Class 4
plan.evidence: Only a trip-report entry (rock climb via West Face-West Rib) found, with no rating; the spire's wrap-around is reported elsewhere as loose Class 3.

headline: WI4
WI4
plan.evidence: AAJ: Wilkes-Booth, Lincoln Peak NW Face, 2,000 ft, IV WI4 (FA March 2015).
SummitPost route page and Lemke both title it 'South Face 5.5', 3 pitches (5.4, 5.5, Class 3); one TR mentions 5.6.

headline: Class 2
Class 2
plan.evidence: Easiest route from the Upper Enchantments is easy Class 2 scrambling (some call it a walk-up).

headline: 3rd-4th class
Class 4
plan.evidence: Easiest route is the Northeast Face, Class 3-4 scrambling; record notes short belayed 3rd-4th class pitches.

before.rock_grade: Class 2-4 (mostly 2-3, short Class 3-4 moves near the summit block)

body.rock_grade: Class 2-3 (loose andesite; short exposed Class 3 summit block)

headline: Class 2-4
Class 3
plan.evidence: MP: 3rd, Mod. Snow; TRs give 400-800 ft of Class 2-3 rock and a short exposed Class 3 summit block. One TR calls the ramp Class 3-4.

before.rock_grade: Low 5th class (several short pitches), Class 3 on the final scramble

body.rock_grade: Class 3 (loose gully-chimney and exposed summit scramble)

headline: Low 5th class
Class 3
plan.evidence: MP: Cowlitz/Ingraham Glaciers 3rd, Steep Snow. The Mountaineers' South Face variant instead climbs several pitches of Class 4-low 5th rock.

before.rock_grade: Class 2-4 (mostly 2-3, short Class 3-4 moves near the summit block)

body.rock_grade: Class 2-3 (loose andesite; short exposed Class 3 summit block)

headline: Class 2-4
Class 3
plan.evidence: Standard Fryingpan/Whitman (East Shoulder) route: MP 3rd, Mod. Snow; short exposed Class 3 summit block.

headline: Class 3
plan.evidence: TR: easy Class 2 ledges to the ridge, an exposed Class 3+ traverse beneath the summit, and a final Class 3 scramble.

body.rock_grade: Class 2-3 (Class 3 on the exposed summit traverse)

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: Class 2 talus to the south (false) summit, then a Class 3 exposed traverse to the true north summit, which is the crux.

headline: Class 4
Class 3
plan.evidence: From Luna Col the broad south ridge is Class 2 talus to the false summit; the traverse to the true summit is Class 3 and the crux.

headline: 5.12b
plan.evidence: MP: 5.12 Grade IV, 11 pitches, crux P7 roof 5.12-; the FA's blog titles it 5.12b.

headline: Steep snow
Class 3
plan.evidence: Banana (NE) Couloir: 2,000 ft of 40-45 degree snow below, 45-50 above, 50 degrees at the very top; booted, with no ice grade.

headline: Class 4
Class 4
plan.evidence: Steep rock and an easy chimney to the notch NW of the summit; rated Class 4.

headline: Class 3-4
Class 4
plan.evidence: South Ridge rated Class 3-4: an easy heather ridge to the false summit, then Class 3-4 broken ledges that corkscrew the summit's east side.

headline: Class 3-4
Class 4
plan.evidence: No route-specific rating found beyond the record's Class 3-4 heather gullies; the neighbouring routes to the same summit are Class 3-4 and Class 4.
From the pocket glacier, cross the schrund (possibly difficult), then shelves to a blocky open book; one 5.6 pitch to a slab.

headline: Class 3
Class 2
plan.evidence: MP: East Ridge 'Easy Snow'; easiest route Class 2; Mountaineers rate it a Basic Glacier Climb. The crux is the exposed snow knife-edge.

headline: WI2-3
AI3
plan.evidence: MP: Northwest Ice Couloir AI2-3 Steep Snow; a fall TR calls it WI3 in lean conditions.

headline: AI2
AI2
plan.evidence: SummitPost: Grade II, several pitches of snow and ice to 60 degrees right of the East Ridge, joining the knife-edge to the summit.
MP: West Arete 5.8, Mod. Snow; TR titles it IV 5.8.

headline: AI2-3
AI2-3
plan.evidence: MP: Eldorado Peak Northwest Ice Couloir AI2-3 Steep Snow.

headline: Class 4
Class 4
plan.evidence: MP: 4th, Mod. Snow, Grade III; Class 4/low-5th rock and a short 60+ degree snow step on the East Ridge. The gully constriction is 45-degree snow early season and melts to 5th-class rock later.

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: SummitPost: easy class-3 route gaining the NW ridge to the notch and summit; one 10-20 ft cliff band with an easy class 3 step; trip reports call the crux class 2/3.

headline: 5.10c
5.10c
plan.evidence: 1960 Cooper-Gordon North Face; modern free ascents report a 5.10c crux pitch (Holsten 2013; Puryear lists 'V 5.10c, 20 pitches').

headline: Class 3-4
Class 3
plan.evidence: SummitPost: the standard (only non-technical) route to the main summit is easy class 3; a trip report calls the crux class 2/3; no source gives class 4.

headline: Class 3-4
Class 4
plan.evidence: SummitPost: West Ridge is the standard Class 4 route; trip report: exposed Class 4 gully ~100 ft below the summit.

headline: 3rd-4th class
Class 3
plan.evidence: West side of the summit block: a couple of class 3 slab moves and one steep move; an easier class 3 gully on the SE side; harder 4th/5th lines are optional.

headline: 4th class
Class 4
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: 4th class, Grade II, Easy Snow; a mellow 3rd-4th class scramble to the exposed summit block after the Terror Glacier snow gully.

headline: AI1-2
AI1-2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: AI1-2 Steep Snow, Grade III; ~1,000 ft of 45-50 degree snow or alpine ice (max ~55), then a broken ridge. Other sources rate it as high as AI3/WI3.

headline: Class 3
Class 4
plan.evidence: The gully to the west ridge starts with steep class 3/4 climbing; reports say the upper 250 ft will 'certainly involve some class 4'; then an exposed ridge crest.
Trip report via the west face/gully: crux 'exposed 5.6 moves' in a dihedral, then chimneys to 5.5; Wikipedia: the standard route is Class 5; WTA report: two low class 5 pitches.
Only description found: ~5 short pitches of loose blocky climbing, finishing with 'wonderful easy climbing up cracks and knobs'; no number given anywhere.

body.rock_grade: 5.3 (one short pitch below the summit ridge)

plan.evidence: SummitPost gives 5.3; Mountaineers: 3rd/4th class with a short mid-5th pitch to the summit-ridge notch; Mountain Project: Easy 5th, 2 pitches.

headline: Class 3
plan.evidence: Easiest (North Col) route: steep snow and a 5.6 chimney (now bolted) to the summit, then a ramp and Class 3 (some avoidable Class 4).

headline: Class 2-3
Class 3
plan.evidence: The easiest route is class 3 scrambling; none of its routes are technical, plus ~45 degree snow in season.

headline: AI2-3
AI3
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: AI2-3 Steep Snow, Grade III, 4,700 ft; moderate snow/ice with short, steeper icefall sections that may need a belay.

headline: Grade III
Class 3
plan.evidence: The Lava Glacier route reaches ~45 degrees on the upper headwall, Grade III; Mountain Project grades the Lava Glacier 'Mod. Snow'. No ice grade given.

headline: AI1-2
Class 3
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Mod. Snow; moderate-to-steep snow and sometimes alpine ice, mostly simul-climbed on pickets; the crux chute near 10,000 ft is 45-65 degrees for ~50 ft.

headline: II
Class 3
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: 'Steep Snow'; a 40 degree glacier, then a 45 degree headwall; an optional 40-ft 60-70 degree snow/ice step below Piker's Peak.

headline: II
Class 3
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: North Ridge 'Mod. Snow'; Grade II+, snow to ~40-50 degrees, with loose class 2-3 rock on the cleaver.

headline: AI1-2
AI2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: North Ridge (West Face) AI1-2 Steep Snow.

headline: F
Class 2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: South Spur 'Easy Snow'; the relatively easy, non-technical standard route.

before.grade: Glacier climb with steep snow and short summit rock

headline: 3rd class
Class 3
plan.evidence: The standard Eel Glacier route is a Grade I, Class 3 glacier climb: a steep snow finger to Flypaper Pass, then Class 3 (3+ near the top) rock to the East Peak.

headline: Class 2-3
Class 3
plan.evidence: Mountaineers alpine scramble: technical difficulty 3; scramble the ridge west from Mount Annette's south ridge to the summit.

headline: AD
Class 2
plan.evidence: SummitPost: a moderate 5,200 ft crevassed glacier climb with a bergschrund to cross, Grade III; no rock or ice grade.

headline: 3rd class
Class 3
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: 'Mod. Snow', not technically difficult; the solid, well-featured rock section is 3rd class with a fixed hand line.

headline: 4th class
AI3
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Cockscomb Ridge T 4th, AI2-3 PG13. No 5th-class rock; the graded crux is AI2-3 ice.

headline: PD
Class 2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Coleman/Deming Glacier 'Mod. Snow'; a non-technical glacier route finishing on the Roman Wall (~35-40 degrees).

headline: AI4
AI4
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: AI4 Steep Snow, Grade IV, 2,000 ft; the lower half is firm snow to 50 degrees, the upper 800 ft is ~60 degree ice.

headline: Grade II
Class 2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Easton Glacier 'Easy Snow'; a broad, moderate glacier climb finishing on the Roman Wall.

headline: WI3
WI3
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: WI3 Steep Snow, Grade III, ~3,000 ft; the crux is the ice cliff/serac step on the ridge.

headline: Grade III
Class 2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project: Squak Glacier 'Easy Snow'; steady snow slopes on the south side up to ~35-40 degrees.

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: The easiest route is class 3 scrambling, finishing with a blocky 3rd class scramble; some east-ridge variants have class 4 sections.

headline: Class 2-3
Class 2
plan.evidence: Wikipedia: the easiest route is class 2 scrambling; the record's own breakdown is Class 2 throughout.

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: The common south summit of Berge is third class from the Berge-Buck saddle; the last 100 ft are mostly class 2 scrambling.

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: From Upper Eagle Lake: talus and scree below the east face, then ~100 ft of exposed Class 3 (two exposed class 3 moves in a gully) to the summit.

headline: 5.8-5.9 R
plan.evidence: SummitPost: North Ridge 5.9, Grade III; ~150 m of 5.8-5.9 R climbing on compact granite to gain the crest.

headline: Class 4
Class 4
plan.evidence: Wikipedia: the standard summit route is a Class 4 scramble via the north slopes, with glaciers on the north and east flanks.

body.rock_grade: Class 2 (Class 3-4 only on the crest toward the Middle Peak)

headline: Class 2-3
Class 2
plan.evidence: Wikipedia: the easiest route is class 2; a long gradual ridge, mostly class 1-2 over false summits; class 3-4 only if staying on the crest toward the Middle Peak.

before.grade: Class 2–3 with steep snow early season

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: SummitPost: the Catwalk is Class 3; the rest of the climb, including the SW ridge, is Class 1-2.

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: The easiest route is a class 3 scramble up the scree-covered south slope; a direct SW rib/gully is sustained class 2/3.
Mountain Project: Challenger Glacier 5.5 Mod. Snow, Grade II; the final summit rock is one pitch of 5.5 (others call it 5.6, or 5.7 in Selected Climbs).

headline: Class 2-3
Class 3
plan.evidence: West Route: a large ramp up the face to the summit ridge, Class 2-3; a west-ridge rock band variant needs a few Class 3-4 moves, plus a steep exposed snowfield near the top.

headline: Class 3-4
Class 4
plan.evidence: Corkscrew route from the Clark-Johnson col on ledges around the S and E sides, finishing with an exposed class 3/4 slot up the north side of the summit block; usually a 60-ft rappel to descend.

headline: Class 2-3
Class 3
plan.evidence: The easiest route is class 2 via the Hayden Pass trail, with a brief stretch of Class 3 scrambling on the west side of the summit.

before.rock_grade: 5.0 (rated Class 3 by consensus, with one low-5th-class move gaining the summit block)

body.rock_grade: Class 3-4 (exposed finger-crack ledge; a few 4th-class moves on the summit block)

headline: Class 4
plan.evidence: The Olympic Mountains climbing guide rates the Finger Traverse 3rd class (a finger crack along a downsloping ledge, often roped); the route to the summit then needs a couple of 4th class moves on the summit block.

headline: Class 3
Class 4
plan.evidence: The South Chute standard route is rated Class 3, Grade II, but sources note a couple of required 4th class moves on the summit block after exposed 3rd class scrambling.

headline: Class 3
Class 4
plan.evidence: The North Chute is rated Class 3+, Grade II; it rejoins the standard route, whose summit block needs a couple of 4th class moves.

headline: Class 3-4
Class 4
plan.evidence: The Terrible Traverse is a 3rd class, steep exposed snow traverse above a cliff on the standard route; the summit block beyond needs a couple of 4th class moves.

before.rock_grade: 5.4 (some parties rate the crux 5.5-5.6 depending on line)

plan.evidence: SummitPost and an NWHikers trip report: West Arete YDS 5.5, Grade III; Mountaineers lists it as Grade III 5.4. Mostly 4th and low 5th, ~1,100 ft.
Abegg (descent): grassy 3rd class ledges with occasional 4th class moves and one or two short 5th class downclimbing moves; no number given.
